name: fallback-swiftshader
description: REALISTIC-SOFTWARE-FALLBACK: the headless runner IS a software rasteriser (SwiftShader), so `deviceClass` detects `weak`, `softwareRenderer` is true, and `softwareRasterFallback` must floor Realistic to a baked-only path. Asserts the RESOLVED settings (shadowMapSize 0, postprocessing false, ao false, dprMax 1) plus the live `gl.shadowMap.enabled`, then shoots both modes from the same default orbit pose. Needs the probe dev server on :5200 (`npx vite --config vite.probe.config.ts --port 5200 --strictPort`) — the resolved-settings snapshot imports `/src/scene/quality.ts`, which only a dev server serves.

steps.name: boot-splash-gone
steps.failMessage: #boot-loader still covering the screen. It is removed from the DOM only once `booting` clears, which depends on sceneReady — measured 751ms and 36604ms across two runs of the SAME scenario, so no fixed wait covers it.

steps.name: dismiss-overlays
steps.eval: try { localStorage.setItem('hdb_onboarded','1') } catch {}; const s = window.__store.getState(); s.endTour?.(); s.setOnboardingOpen?.(false); s.dismissLocationPrompt?.()

steps.name: software-rasteriser-detected
steps.failMessage: The runner is not reporting a software rasteriser. This scenario is only meaningful under SwiftShader — check the browser was NOT launched with a real GPU (SHOT_GPU=1 defeats it).

steps.name: device-class-weak
steps.failMessage: deviceClass is not `weak` under a software rasteriser — `deviceClassFor` name-matching regressed.

steps.name: snapshot-resolved-quality
steps.eval: (async () => { const m = await import('/src/scene/quality.ts'); const s = window.__store.getState(); window.__q = m.resolveQuality(s.qualityTier, s.qualityOverrides, s.deviceClass, s.softwareRenderer); })()

steps.name: realistic-floored

waitFor.store: state.qualityTier === 'realistic' && !!window.__q && window.__q.shadowMapSize === 0 && window.__q.postprocessing === false && window.__q.ao === false && window.__q.dof === false && window.__q.cinematic === false && window.__q.dprMax === 1

steps.failMessage: Realistic did NOT fall back on a software rasteriser — the resolved settings still carry shadows/post/AO/DPR2. Check the `softwareRasterFallback` flag and `resolveQuality`.

steps.name: baked-gi-still-on
steps.failMessage: The fallback dropped the IBL probe / shrank the env map past the measured floor. Baked light is the whole point of the fallback path.

steps.name: no-shadow-casting-light-in-scene

waitFor.store: (() => { const sc = window.__three?.scene; if (!sc) return false; let casters = 0; sc.traverse((o) => { if (o.isLight && o.castShadow) casters++ }); return casters === 0 })()

steps.failMessage: A light is still casting shadows under the software fallback. NOTE: the Canvas `shadows` prop keeps `gl.shadowMap.enabled` true at every tier (r3f re-applies it every render), so the shadow map is switched off per-LIGHT via `castShadow={shadowMapSize > 0}` — that is what this asserts.

steps.name: device-pixel-ratio-clamped-to-1
steps.failMessage: The renderer is still drawing above DPR 1 — the `dprMax` floor did not reach `QualityController`'s clamp.
